newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB shares fall after full-yr results.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB shares fall after full-yr results.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc fell 11 pence to 459, after the satellite TV broadcaster reported full-year profits at the lower end of analysts expectations.
"The results are at the bottom end of forecast but they were not particularly disappointing," one market maker said. Other market makers said they were surprised by the BSkyB share weakness.
British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc said pre-tax profit for the year to June 30 rose 22 percent to 313.7 million stg.
The figure was boosted by a one-off 14 million stg contribition stemming from a deal to supply programmes to a new British TV service formed by Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group.
"The underlying figure was a little bit near the bottom of the range," said analyst Louise Barton at Henderson Crosthwaite.
She added she would not alter her forecast for current year profits, predicting flat pre-tax figures for the 12 months to June 30, 1998.
BSkyB shares, meanwhile, recouped most of their earlier losses, trading down 3-1/2 pence at 466-1/2 by 0733 GMT.
